The whole Bay Area · times verified Sept 14

This Week in the Bay

Tuesday–Sunday, September 15–20, 2026 · SF · East Bay · South Bay · North Bay

The week the fall season lands all at once. Fort Mason opens seven galleries in one night, SF Open Studios starts its 52nd year, the Symphony plays its first subscription weekend, Chinatown holds its 36th Autumn Moon Festival — and Flower Piano’s twelve pianos come out of the Botanical Garden for the last time on Sunday. Sectioned by type and ranked within each. Filter by day and by region.

🎨 Fort Mason Art Walk + SF Open Studios opening weekend 🎵 Flower Piano’s final three days 🌂 Autumn Moon Festival, Chinatown 🎪 Bay Area Theatre Week (to 60% off, code BATW2026) ☀️ Fri is the clear night — Sat/Sun cloud over ⚠️ SF Opera dark: orchestra on strike

Top 5 This Week

The five best things happening across every category — chosen for rarity and variety, not for being the biggest. Four of the five are gone by Monday.
01 · IMMERSIVE CIRCUS

The Soiled Dove — with Joan Baez

Fri 9/18 & Sat 9/19 · dinner 7:30pm, show 9pm · The Big Top at Radium Runway, Alameda Point · $75–$214, 21+
Vau de Vire’s 1890s Barbary Coast dinner-circus under a 12,000 sq ft Italian big top — aerial, vaudeville, burlesque and original ragtime, with Joan Baez in a rare staged theatrical role. She is out for the 9/26–27 shows, so this weekend is the one. Costume encouraged.
02 · ART · FREE

Fort Mason Fall Art Walk

Thu 9/17 · 5:00–8:30pm · Fort Mason Center, Marina, SF · Free (register for a drink ticket)
Seven opening receptions on one waterfront campus in one evening: Haines’ eight-artist 250 Years, Indigenous Futures (talks at 7), FOR-SITE in the 1901 Guardhouse, Leah Rosenberg’s new mural across eighteen loading docks, and SF Camerawork reopening after announcing its closure in August and being rescued weeks later. Plus Magic Theatre micro-performances every five minutes.
03 · MUSIC · OUTDOORS

Flower Piano — final weekend

Fri 9/18–Sun 9/20 · 10am–6pm daily · SF Botanical Garden, Golden Gate Park · Free for SF residents; $18 otherwise
Twelve grand pianos hidden across fifty-five acres for eleven days a year, with 130 scheduled performances — and between them, anyone may sit down and play. Sunday 9/20 is the last day, closing with Oakland pianist Kev Choice. The de Young is free the same Saturday, three minutes’ walk away.
04 · JAZZ

Ravi Coltrane — Coltrane Centennial

Sun 9/20 · doors 6:30pm, show 7:30pm · Raven Theater, Healdsburg · $31–$106  |  Sat 9/19 at the UC Theatre, Berkeley is sold out
John Coltrane would have turned 100 this month, and his son is marking it. KQED picked both nights; Berkeley is gone, so Healdsburg on Sunday is the way in — the quartet with Jonathan Finlayson, in a 500-seat room, wine country out the door.
05 · ODDITY

GODWAFFLENOISEPANCAKES

Sat 9/19 · 12:00–2:00pm · Center for New Music, 55 Taylor St, Tenderloin, SF · $10 / $6 members
Twenty-six years of noon-time noise shows where the ten-dollar ticket also buys you free gourmet vegan pancakes. This edition: Dimmer (Hammer/Dimuzio), Medicine Cabinet, Connor Tomaka, Impact Design. It is over by 2pm, which leaves the whole rest of Saturday.

Classical, Jazz & Chamber

10 concerts

⚠ SF Opera is not in this guide. The SF Opera Orchestra went on strike 35 minutes before the season-opening curtain on Sept 12; opening night and Opera in the Park were cancelled and, as of Sept 14, talks are stalled with Thursday’s Simon Boccanegra in doubt. Nothing at the War Memorial is safe to recommend this week — check sfopera.com before making plans. Also worth knowing: the Symphony’s Opening Gala with Hilary Hahn is next Thursday, Sept 24, not this weekend.

🎹
TOP PICK★ SF Classical Voice
SymphonicFri 9/18 & Sat 9/19
7:30pm

Garrick Ohlsson Plays Brahms

Davies Symphony Hall · Civic Center
San Francisco
From ~$102 · Inside Music talk before

The whole programme orbits Robert and Clara Schumann: Unsuk Chin’s subito con forza answering Beethoven, then Brahms’s First Concerto as elegy with Ohlsson — the definitive American Brahmsian — and Schumann’s Fourth with the Clara theme running through it. David Afkham’s first subscription weekend here, and SFCV ran a spotlight on him for exactly these nights.

Theater

9 shows

Mid-September is the gap between the summer closings and the wave of season openers that lands Sept 22–26 — A.C.T., SF Playhouse, Shotgun and Z Space are all dark this week. What’s left is unusually good anyway: a world premiere, a West Coast premiere, four new-play readings and two shows in their final performances. Bay Area Theatre Week runs through Sun 9/20 — up to 60% off at 40+ companies with code BATW2026.

🍲

African Stew

Magic Theatre, Fort Mason Bldg D · Marina
San Francisco

Lisa B. Thompson’s world premiere for the Lorraine Hansberry Theatre: a Black American woman and her Nigerian fiancé’s families collide over a single dinner in Oakland. The Chronicle found it “richest in family conflict”; KQED and 48 Hills both flagged it. Fort Mason means dinner is solved.

Dance

6 shows

SF Ballet is on tour and CounterPulse’s September calendar is genuinely empty (checked), so the week belongs to the smaller companies — which this time means a season opener with a world premiere, a touring Palestinian troupe, and an immersive quintet in a 1625 Bush St studio.

Grace Cathedral · Nob Hill

Harmonic sensors pick up the cathedral’s carillon bells and organ pipes vibrating without being played, and amplify them into the nave. A major sound artist turning a Gothic building into an instrument of itself — restorative and avant-garde at the same time, in the middle of a weekday.

Notes & things to double-check

Every date and time here was read off the venue’s own event page on September 14, 2026. Confirm these before you go: SF Opera is omitted entirely — the orchestra struck on Sept 12, two performances are already cancelled and talks were still stalled on the 14th; Lick Observatory lists Fri 9/18 on its own site but these tours sell out, so book before you drive to Mt Hamilton; Audium runs Fri and Sat only this cycle — there is no Thursday show, despite what some listings say; Chabot and Foothill telescope nights are clear-sky-only and Saturday looks cloudy, so treat Friday as the night; Cal Academy’s Osher Rainforest is closed for maintenance Sept 15–17 and may not reopen for Thursday’s NightLife; the Exploratorium’s Tactile Dome is closed through Sept 28; MoAD is closed through Sept 29; Tabemasho’s 2026 ticket price isn’t published anywhere — call the JCCCNC; and Patti Smith, Takes All Kinds, Tantrum Yoga and the Berkeley Ravi Coltrane show are all sold out (waitlists and returns only). A few cards carry no image because the venue is bot-walled or ships no share image — those show the clean category gradient.

Deliberately deprioritized or skipped

Per your anti-preferences: EDM and DJ club nights (DNA’s own Fri/Sat programming, Steve Aoki’s Dim Mak night, The Tech’s “LASERS: EDM”), arena and stadium shows (J. Cole at Oakland Arena, T-Pain in Golden Gate Park, Jack Harlow, Brandi Carlile at Frost), sports (Golden State Valkyries, the Aloha Run), bar crawls and drinking-as-event (Oktoberfest on Front, the Elmwood Wine Walk), and expos (the Oddities & Curiosities Expo, Center Hardware’s Toolapalooza). Pride- and identity-framed programming was checked and set aside rather than featured: the Castro Night Market finale, Pride in Martinez, Southern Exposure’s Unity Fest (a strong roster — McGee, Johanson, McCarthy — but queer-skateboarding framed), NCTC’s Little Shop, the Roxie’s OUTlook strand titles and the SF Drag King Contest. Also out on recurrence, having been checked rather than assumed: Downtown First Thursdays, Valencia Live, both Bike Parties, the Alameda Point Antiques Faire and Oakland Vintage Market (all first- or second-week), and Sunday Streets, which has no September route day at all.

What was unreachable this run

Visit Oakland’s arts calendar rendered an empty shell and its underlying API is edge-blocked, so that aggregator contributed nothing; Niles Essanay’s silent-comedy night on 16mm and 35mm with live music is real and confirmed via the Film on Film celluloid calendar, but the museum’s site is a JavaScript app with no linkable event page, so it isn’t carded here; and the Oakland Review of Books’ weekly literary calendar publishes on Tuesdays, so its Sept 15–20 edition landed after this sweep.
